description: Data dictionary for the TrueNorth S&P 500 values-investing dataset. Each scored field on a company record is an object of shape { value, source, source_url, confidence, notes, last_updated }. confidence is one of High (primary-source verified), Medium (documented but requires interpretation), Low (indirect/sector-level inference), or None (no verifiable data found -- never a fabricated placeholder). Confidence levels are used internally by the TrueNorth app and are not shown directly to survey respondents.

confidence_levels.High: Primary-source verified (e.g. a specific SEC filing, EPA/OSHA/NLRB record, or SIC code lookup).
confidence_levels.Medium: Documented but requires interpretation (e.g. business description implies involvement without an exact figure).
confidence_levels.Low: Indirect or sector-level inference (e.g. peer/sector benchmarking, no company-specific record).
confidence_levels.None: No verifiable data found via an approved source. value is the literal string 'No verifiable data found'.

scored_field_shape.value: The score/answer itself. Type varies by field (boolean, enum string, number, or descriptive string).
scored_field_shape.source: Human-readable name of the specific source used (e.g. 'SEC 10-K Item 1 Business, FY2024', 'EPA ECHO enforcement case #...').
scored_field_shape.source_url: Direct URL (or API endpoint + query) used to retrieve the value.
scored_field_shape.confidence: One of High | Medium | Low | None.
scored_field_shape.notes: Optional free-text interpretation notes, caveats, or context (e.g. flagging a recent merger distorting a figure).
scored_field_shape.last_updated: ISO 8601 date the field was last verified/populated.

top_level_fields.ticker: Exchange ticker symbol, as listed by Wikipedia's S&P 500 constituents table.
top_level_fields.cik: SEC EDGAR Central Index Key, 10-digit zero-padded string. Used as the key for all SEC EDGAR lookups.
top_level_fields.date_added_to_sp500: Date the company was added to the S&P 500 index, if listed by Wikipedia.
top_level_fields.founded_year: Year the company (or a listed predecessor) was founded, if listed by Wikipedia.

recent_corporate_action_flag.description: True if the company underwent a merger, spin-off, IPO, or major restructuring within the trailing 12 months. Per TrueNorth methodology, single-year revenue/return comparisons for such companies are unreliable and must be flagged rather than silently scored (see EXE/Expand Energy case in background doc).

top_level_fields.processing_status: pending | in_progress | complete | manual_review_needed -- tracked here and mirrored in logs/progress.json.

q21_countries_of_concern.survey_question: Avoiding companies operating in specific countries or regions of concern
q21_countries_of_concern.value_type: array of country names (possibly empty) or 'No verifiable data found'
sources: 10-K Item 1/1A text scan for an OFAC-comprehensively-sanctioned country name near real operational-presence language
SEC Section 13(r) of the Exchange Act (Iran/Syria disclosure requirement)
q21_countries_of_concern.note: Implemented 2026-08-20 -- see find_countries_of_concern() in scripts/lib.py. The XBRL Frames API originally proposed here turned out not to expose per-company dimensional geographic-segment breakdowns (only company-wide scalar totals), so this uses the 10-K text scan instead. Deliberately narrow country list (Russia, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Belarus, Venezuela -- OFAC's comprehensively-sanctioned jurisdictions) rather than an editorial judgment call about broader geopolitical concern (e.g. does not include China). Section 13(r) presence is High confidence (a purpose-built mandatory disclosure item -- a company only includes it when it has actual Iran/Syria-connected activity); a context-matched country name without Section 13(r) is Medium; an empty result (no match at all) is Low, not None, since the company's own 10-K was successfully searched.

q22_data_privacy_practices.survey_question: Companies with strong data privacy practices
q22_data_privacy_practices.value_type: object: { item_1_05_incident_count, examples } or 'No verifiable data found'
sources: SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov), scoped to the company's own CIK, for 8-K Item 1.05 filings
q22_data_privacy_practices.note: Implemented 2026-08-20 -- see cybersecurity_incident_search() in scripts/lib.py. SEC Litigation Releases (the source originally proposed here) are not indexed by EDGAR full-text search (which only covers filings, not the separate litigation microsite) and have no other free structured API, so this uses Item 1.05 instead -- the SEC rule (effective December 2023) requiring disclosure of a material cybersecurity incident within four business days. Because the search is scoped to the company's own CIK rather than a name-matched search across all filers, a zero result is a real, meaningful answer (Low confidence) rather than a failed match -- though Item 1.05 only covers incidents from December 2023 onward.

q24_founder_family.value_type: founder_led: boolean (true only if founder/co-founder currently holds CEO or Exec Chairman); family_owned: boolean + ownership_pct (true only if founding family retains a documented significant ownership/voting stake)
q24_founder_family.note: Must show real variation across companies, not default to false. This was a known pipeline bug in the prior dataset per background doc.

q25_industry_personal_tie.survey_question: Supporting companies in industries the client has personal/professional ties to
q25_industry_personal_tie.note: This question is about the client, not the company. Satisfied by accurate gics_sector/gics_sub_industry tagging already captured at top level.

q26_27_derived_risk_profile.value_type: growth_potential driven by revenue_growth_pct and five_year_total_return_pct; stability driven by beta/volatility, dividend_consistency, debt_to_equity
sources: Finnhub free tier (finnhub.io) -- requires API key, currently unavailable, see manual_review_needed.md

additional_criteria.description: Real, populated fields that exist on every company record but are NOT one of the 27 official survey questions from the founding materials -- see data/candidate_additional_criteria.json for the full proposal/review record. Kept out of `questions` above so the numbered 1-27 schema the app repo may depend on stays unchanged.

women_led.value_type: boolean (true if the current CEO is a woman) or 'No verifiable data found'
sources: DEF 14A proxy statement (EDGAR) -- see find_ceo_gender_signal() in scripts/lib.py
women_led.note: Identifies the CEO's surname via a name-immediately-before-title regex, then reads which honorific (Mr./Ms./Mrs.) or, failing that, which pronoun (she/her vs he/his) the filing itself consistently uses for that specific named person -- never inferred from a first name. Low confidence, same class of flattened-text heuristic as founder_led/family_owned; the matched surname and evidence quote are always shown in notes for spot-checking.
